Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below plus three short attachments (measurement brief, Grafana invite instructions, and the SLA Adjustment Form used to request temporary waivers). If you want a 30-minute walkthrough of the dashboards, happy to schedule next week.

Summary answers (high-level):

- SLOs reported: Availability (successful API responses for model inference) measured as monthly uptime percentage (target 99.95% for dedicated plans, 99.9% for hosted) and latency SLOs expressed as p95 and p99 for request-response time at the API gateway (we publish p95/p99 for text-generation and embedding endpoints).

- Measurement approach: Primary SLIs are derived from server-side telemetry (success/error codes + request timing). We supplement with synthetic probing from three regions to catch regional regressions. Errors exclude client-side rate-limited requests and malformed payloads; we maintain an error taxonomy in the measurement brief. Aggregation windows: rolling 30-day and calendar-month; thresholds for contractual SLA use calendar-month.

- Monitoring stack & access: Metrics stored in Prometheus long-term storage, dashboards in Grafana. We can provide a read-only Grafana link scoped to your account and a daily CSV export of the SLO time series for audit purposes (attachments and link provided). Retention: 13 months full resolution, 3 years aggregated.

- Alerting & incident workflow: Alerts are emitted from Prometheus -> Alertmanager -> PagerDuty; standard thresholds are p95 > SLA_target * 1.25 for latency and availability dips > 0.5% absolute over a 1-hour window for critical alerts. On-call rotation and runbooks are included in the measurement brief.

- Evidence for audits: We can produce historical graphs, CSV exports of the underlying SLI time series, raw tracer IDs for sample traces, and signed attestations for the measurement methodology.

- Temporary waiver process: To request a temporary allowance (e.g., for a planned migration), customers submit the SLA Adjustment Form (attached). Requests require 72-hour notice, impact assessment, and Ops sign-off. For short windows (<=8 hours) we can issue a timeboxed waiver with compensating mitigations (canary routing, prefilling KV caches, temporary increase in instance pool).

Next steps: I attached the measurement brief (slo-measurement-brief.pdf), grafana invite instructions (grafana-readonly-invite.txt) and the SLA Adjustment Form (sla-adjustment-form.pdf). If that covers it, please confirm the migration window dates and we'll start a waiver request internally.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
